hook_text: In 1660, Khoikhoi leaders asked the Dutch a question South Africa is still answering: by what right did you take our land?
clip_script: For the Khoikhoi, land was shared, grazed season by season. For the colonists, land could be owned, fenced and sold. That clash of ideas began in 1657, on Khoikhoi grazing land along the Liesbeek River. Then came wars, cattle raids, smallpox, trekboers spreading inland and commandos attacking the San. Step by step, over one hundred and fifty years, the Khoikhoi and San lost their land, their herds and their independence. Many ended up working on farms that had once been their grazing grounds. Today, land is still one of South Africa's biggest questions.
visual_style: An open landscape with grazing cattle is gradually divided by hedges and fences; a map shows the colony's boundary moving outward; a final close-up of a title deed.
pacing: Slow, step by step, with a pause on the final question.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson on land dispossession at the Cape.
